references.text: Verse 40 identifies Andrew as one of the two disciples who heard John the Baptist's testimony about Jesus and followed him, as described in [ref:Joh 1:35-37|John 1:35-37].
Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, is also mentioned at the feeding miracle, where he brings the boy with five loaves and two fish to Jesus ([ref:Joh 6:8|John 6:8]).
Andrew appears again together with Philip when Greeks wish to meet Jesus, showing his role as a mediator between people and Jesus ([ref:Joh 12:22|John 12:22]).
Matthew tells of the calling of Andrew and Simon Peter by the Sea of Galilee, where they were fishermen and were called to become fishers of men ([ref:Matt 4:18-20|Matthew 4:18-20]).
Mark's account of the calling of Andrew and Simon by the sea, where they left their nets and followed Jesus ([ref:Mark 1:16-18|Mark 1:16-18]).
Andrew is mentioned as the brother of Simon, and they shared a house in Capernaum, confirming the relationship noted in John 1:40 ([ref:Mark 1:29|Mark 1:29]).
In the list of the twelve apostles, Andrew is named together with his brother Simon Peter as the first ones ([ref:Matt 10:2|Matthew 10:2]).
